sections.h2: Where is Medford, Oregon, and what is the land like?
sections.html:
Medford is the county seat of Jackson County, in the Rogue Valley about 27 miles north of the California border. It sits at 1,434 feet in a rain shadow between the Cascade Range and the Siskiyou Mountains, which explains the dry summers.

Roxy Ann Peak rises to 3,576 feet at the edge of town, and Prescott Park around it covers 1,740 acres. Bear Creek Park runs nearly 100 acres, and Alba Park, deeded to the city in 1888, is the oldest. Houses on the foothills and houses on the valley floor face different slopes, drainage and fire exposure, so describe the lot as well as the building.

sections.h2: How did Medford get its start?
sections.html:
Medford began as a railroad survey stop. Surveyors working on the Oregon and California Railroad route in 1883 included David Loring, who named the town for Medford, Massachusetts.

  • The town was platted in early December 1883 with 82 blocks.
  • The first post office opened February 6, 1884.
  • Medford incorporated as a town on February 24, 1885, and as a city in 1905.
  • It took the county seat from Jacksonville in 1927.
  • Interstate 5 was completed through town in 1967.

That timeline matters for sellers because it explains the mix of old railroad-era streets near downtown and newer subdivisions farther out.

sections.html:

sections.h2: Which employers drive the Medford economy?
sections.html:
Health care is the largest driver. Asante Rogue Regional Medical Center and Providence Medford Medical Center together employ more than 2,000 people.

  • Harry and David is described as the largest employer in Southern Oregon, with about 1,700 year-round and 6,700 seasonal workers.
  • Lithia Motors, a Fortune 500 company, has been headquartered in Medford since 1970.
  • Jackson County has more than 10,000 acres of orchards and shares the Rogue Valley and Applegate wine appellations with Josephine County.

With seasonal work at Harry and David and shift work in health care, a rental's tenant mix can turn over on a different calendar than a typical house, so check lease end dates before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How hot and dry does Medford get, and what does that do to a house?
sections.html:
Medford has a Mediterranean climate with hot summers and dry air. Summers average 61 afternoons above 90 degrees and 11 above 100, and the record high is 115 degrees, reached July 20, 1946 and again June 28, 2021.

Annual precipitation averages 18.43 inches and snowfall 3.4 inches. Winter temperature inversions can hold fog in the valley for weeks. Long hot spells age roofing, exterior paint and air conditioning equipment, and a buyer's inspector will look at all three.

sections.h2: How did the Almeda fire affect Medford housing?
sections.html:
The Almeda fire started the morning of September 8, 2020, and swept through the Rogue Valley within hours. Jefferson Public Radio reported more than 2,600 homes destroyed between Ashland, Talent, Phoenix and Medford, calling it the most destructive wildfire in Oregon's recorded history.

Medford lost homes too, including a mobile home park in the city. A year later, thousands of displaced residents had not received the federal help they needed to rebuild. For a seller, the effects show up in two ways:

  • Fire-damaged or rebuilt properties may carry insurance, permit or valuation questions that a buyer will ask about.
  • Under ORS 308.146, a fire or other act of God that cuts a property's real market value also reduces its maximum assessed value for that year.

Oregon lawmakers passed a bill in 2025 to repeal the state's contested wildfire hazard map, which the statewide defensible space and building code requirements relied on. A 2023 state law still bars insurers from using a state agency's wildfire hazard map to cancel, decline to renew or raise premiums on a homeowner policy.

sections.h2: How do Medford's highways, buses and airport work?
sections.html:
Interstate 5 runs through the center of Medford, including a 3,229-foot viaduct, and Highways 99, 62 and 238 also serve the city. Rogue Valley International-Medford Airport is Oregon's third-busiest and handles over a million passengers a year on about 60 daily flights.

The Rogue Valley Transportation District has run buses since 1975 and operates eight routes. There is no passenger train service, and the last direct rail service to Portland ended in 1956. Buyers who rely on the bus or the airport may care how close a house is to those lines.

sections.h2: How does Medford fit into the wider Rogue Valley?
sections.html:
Medford is the largest of Jackson County's 11 incorporated cities. The county covers 2,802 square miles, and nearby towns include Ashland, Phoenix, Talent, Central Point and Jacksonville.

Jacksonville was the first county seat, from 1853, and lost ground after the railroad bypassed it. Bear Creek and its watershed lie wholly inside the county and drain to the Rogue River. Buyers often compare Medford with those neighbors, so know what sets your street apart.

Medford School District 549C serves the city, with more than 13,000 students as of 2012. It runs North Medford, South Medford and Central Medford high schools plus Medford Innovation Academy, three middle schools (Hedrick, Oakdale and McLoughlin) and 14 elementary schools.

Private schools include St. Mary's, Cascade Christian, Crossroads and Rogue Valley Adventist. Rogue Community College opened a downtown campus in 1997. Confirm current boundaries with the district before you cite a school in a listing.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Medford housing?
sections.html:
Medford has a lower owner-occupancy rate than nearby McMinnville or Oregon City, at 56.3%. That leaves a large renter base and many landlord-owned houses.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Medford?
sections.html:
Jackson County bills Medford property tax, and the Assessor's Office can be reached at 541-774-6059. The county's address is 10 S Oakdale Ave in Medford.

State law sets the schedule: November 15, February 15 and May 15. Pay by November 15 and you get 3% off the full bill or 2% off if you pay two-thirds. Unpaid balances accrue interest at 1 1/3% per month. ORS 306.815 generally bars cities and counties from taxing transfers of real property, with narrow exceptions, so ask your title company to confirm there is no local transfer charge on your sale.

sections.h2: What do Medford sellers need to plan for?
sections.html:
• A signed disclosure statement for each buyer who makes a written offer, unless the sale is excluded, for example a court-appointed personal representative selling an estate.
  • Smoke, heat or fire history that insurers or buyers may ask about.
  • Tenant notice and move-out timing if the house is a rental.
  • Proration of the current tax year at closing.

A cash buyer can often work around a house's condition, but each buyer sets its own terms, so compare them in writing.

faqs.q: What county is Medford, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Medford is in Jackson County and has been the county seat since 1927. Property tax questions go to the Jackson County Assessor's Office.

faqs.q: How many people live in Medford?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 86,494 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 85,824.

faqs.q: Was Medford affected by the Almeda fire?
faqs.a: Yes. The fire began September 8, 2020, and destroyed more than 2,600 homes across Ashland, Talent, Phoenix and Medford, including a mobile home park in Medford.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Jackson County?
faqs.a: The three installments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. Paying in full by November 15 earns a 3% discount.

faqs.q: Does Medford charge a real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: Generally no. ORS 306.815 bars cities and counties from imposing a transfer tax, with narrow exceptions tied to rules in place on March 31, 1997 or to low recording fees. Your title company can confirm for your sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Medford rental with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers accept occupied houses, but notice rules and lease terms still apply, so confirm them before you set a closing date.
